about: SHA-256 of each prompt template file, with line endings normalised to LF. negsim refuses to load a template whose file no longer matches. A template is frozen once it is listed here: new wording means a new version, never an edit.

gamechat_task_v1.note: GameChat replication (C1): the paper's prompt with the consensus sentence replaced by the JSON stance format.

rulegen_common_v1.note: Rule generation (issue #30): the rule format, the generated field glossary (its hash pinned inside) and the placeholder format example, shared word for word by conditions A and B.

rulegen_negotiate_v1.note: Rule generation, condition A (issue #30): two people negotiate a standing rule; first-person situation; turns of message, proposal, accept, no_rule_possible.

rulegen_state_v1.note: Rule generation, condition B (issue #30): one model states a rule; third-person situation with both people's private information; reply of rule and reason.

rulegen_common_v2.note: Rule generation (issue #32): version 1 for rule format 3: the passage fields, true or false values, the directive field back_up and its consistency rule; the single-file encounter now also covers a stretch the two are in. Its generated glossary's hash is pinned inside.

rulegen_negotiate_v2.note: Rule generation, condition A (issue #32): version 1 with lines for standing still, for being inside a single-file stretch (how far in, how far to each end, how far in the other is), and for each person's fictional group when the session shows it. Uses rulegen_common_v2.

rulegen_state_v2.note: Rule generation, condition B (issue #32): version 1 with the same added lines as rulegen_negotiate_v2, told from outside. Uses rulegen_common_v2.

scenario_passing_v1.note: Track #55 Step 1 (issue #57, RF-2): the description side of the passing scenarios of rounds 1 to 3: rulegen_negotiate_v2's place lines word for word, and the events other_passes, other_stops, i_am_out_of_the_stretch (docs/resolution.md, D1, D16).

resolve_v1.note: Track #55 Step 1 (issue #57, RF-2): the core template, one section per condition (independent, non_verbal, talk); fixed text (role, instructions, reply format, step format with the scenario's events), then the description of D2 with lines for every block, then the decision-point wrapper. No priority field, no convention wording (docs/resolution.md, D1 to D3).

resolve_debrief_v1.note: Track #55 Step 1 (issue #57, RF-2): the debrief of docs/resolution.md, D8, word for word, outside the role, after the agent's last decision point; none is a perfectly good answer.

resolve_v2.note: Track #55, issue #73 (RF-17): resolve_v1 word for word plus the lines a view built from the running simulation needs: an unseen speaker's rough direction and distance band, a signal on a short line, and what came of an earlier decision (moved sideways, further back, steps replaced). The system message is resolve_v1's, byte for byte.

resolve_factors_v1.note: Track #55, issue #60 (RF-5): the lines of the seven core factors (self in ABOUT YOU, other in WHO YOU CAN SEE for the observable three, a designed note in YOUR NOTES) and of the situational factors surroundings and time_of_day (WHERE YOU ARE, the same for everyone); placed verbatim by resolve_v2. The issue's lines, with the place words made scenario-neutral (D16).

resolve_pairwise_v1.note: Track #55, issue #61 (RF-6): the lines of the pairwise perception factors, perceived attractiveness (a matrix: who looks, who is seen) and familiarity (the same for both); placed verbatim by resolve_v2 under the seen person, in the observer's own view only. Issue #61's lines, word for word; with a switch on both levels have a line.

resolve_v3.note: Track #55, issue #61 (RF-6), the user's decision of 2026-10-23: resolve_v2 word for word plus seen_short_extra, which prints a person's factor lines (RF-5's observable ones, RF-6's pairwise ones) under the short line of someone 5 to 10 m away too. Under resolve_v2 no factor line reached an agent in the head-on case, where every decision point is beyond 5 m. The system message is resolve_v2's, byte for byte.

resolve_v4.note: Track #55, issue #64 (RF-9), the user's decision of 2026-10-24 (WORK_LOG-61.md, open question 7): resolve_v3 word for word plus seen_short_age and seen_short_gender, worded as seen_age and seen_gender, which print the other person's age and gender (when visible) under the short line of someone 5 to 10 m away too. Under resolve_v3 neither agent was told the other's age or gender in the head-on case, where every decision point is beyond 5 m. The system message is resolve_v3's, byte for byte.

resolve_v5.note: Track #55, issue #64 (RF-9), the user's decision of 2026-10-24: resolve_v4 word for word except two sentences of the step format, so that any step may have a start (after_seconds counted from the decision; while a later step waits, the agent walks on), and later_step_start: true for the reply parser. In the first 12 paid pilot sessions under resolve_v4, 34 of 81 replies were unreadable because a later step had a start. The description and the retry are resolve_v4's.

resolve_factors_v2.note: Track #55 (issue #92, RF-26): resolve_factors_v1 word for word, plus the lines of real ethnicity: a person's own group in ABOUT YOU and what someone who sees them is told (when ethnicity_visible is on), for Chinese, Malay, Indian and Others; the wording of Others is the user's choice of 2026-10-24 (docs/ethnicity.md).

resolve_v6.note: Track #55, issue #65 (RF-10), decided on the user's delegation of 2026-10-24 (RF-9's recommendation): resolve_v5 word for word except the step format's sentence on until (an until may be {"at_distance_m": <metres>}; an event is written as its name in quotes) and two headings (opposite_drifting, same_drifting: a walking person up to 45 degrees off opposite or same is drifting, not walking across); until_at_distance and until_event_as_object for the reply parser. In RF-9's pilot 58 of 63 unreadable sends were these until forms, and 28 of 30 agents told of a drift as walking across reasoned about a crossing.

resolve_v7.note: Track #55, issue #98 (RF-27), the user's decisions of 2026-10-25: resolve_v6 word for word except three view lines (seen_line_offset and seen_on_line: where the centre of someone ahead is against the straight line ahead of the agent, to 0.1 m, from 10 m; seen_short_body: the other's width from 10 m) and direction_ahead_deg 1 (straight ahead only within 1 degree, not 5). The reply parser is unchanged. RF-10: 116 of 192 head-on sessions collided, 49 with both stepping towards the same wall.

resolve_v8.note: Track #55, issue #101 (RF-29), the user's decisions of 2026-10-25: resolve_v6 word for word except the step format's sidestep key ({"to": left or right, "metres": more than 0 up to 3}: move that far aside at the step's turn angle, or 30 degrees, then walk on parallel) and the until sentence's exception (a step that sidesteps needs no until); the sidestep flag for the reply parser. Turning by degrees stays. In RF-10, RF-27 and RF-28 the sidesteps, planned in degrees and seconds, were too small.

extract_v1.note: Track #55, issue #66 (RF-11): the rule extractor of Step 2. One call reads one encounter type's resolved sessions (an agent table, the other's factors as told), the failed sessions counted, the factor levels, the coin-flip cells and 10 to 20 resolved sessions in full, and writes rules in a YAML block with references, debrief support and a predict list over the table's columns. The instructions are the issue's task 3, the reply fields its task 4; ethnicity and perceived attractiveness are in the table and no rule may read them.

translate_v1.note: Issue #67 (RF-12): the translator of an extracted rule into rule format 3; uses rulegen_common_v2 for the format, word for word.
